📊 Difficulty: Easy

🥘 Ingredients

  • 6 large fresh banana peppers, sliced into 1/4 inch rings
  • 1 1/2 cups white vinegar
  • 1 cup water
  • 2 tablespoons sugar
  • 1 tablespoon kosher salt
  • 1 teaspoon mustard seeds
  • 1 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 2 cloves garlic, smashed
  • 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by washing and slicing your banana peppers into even 1/4 inch rings. This ensures they pickle evenly and absorb the brine properly. Removing the seeds is optional, but leaving some in adds a nice mild heat. Place the sliced peppers in a clean glass jar or bowl. The even size helps the vinegar soak in uniformly, which is key for consistent flavor and texture.
  2. In a saucepan, combine the white vinegar, water, sugar, kosher salt, mustard seeds, black peppercorns, smashed garlic, and red pepper flakes if using. Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sugar and salt. Boiling extracts the flavors from the spices and creates a balanced brine that will preserve the peppers and infuse them with tangy, spicy notes.
  3. Carefully pour the hot brine over the sliced banana peppers in the jar, making sure they are fully submerged. Use a clean utensil to press down the peppers gently if needed. Leaving air pockets can cause uneven pickling or spoilage, so this step is important to ensure all peppers are covered.
  4. Seal the jar tightly with a lid and let it cool to room temperature before placing it in the refrigerator. Cooling prevents condensation inside the jar which can dilute the brine or encourage bacterial growth. Refrigerate for at least 24 hours before tasting, but the peppers will improve in flavor over several days.
  5. After 24 hours, test a pepper ring for flavor and texture. If it’s not tangy enough, let it pickle longer. The longer they sit, the more the flavors meld and the peppers soften slightly while retaining crunch. Use within 2-3 weeks for best quality.
  6. When ready to serve, drain the peppers or add them directly to sandwiches, salads, or antipasto platters. The brine can be reused for another batch if strained and boiled again. This keeps the flavor consistent and reduces waste.
  7. If you want a spicier kick, increase the red pepper flakes or add a few sliced jalapeños to the jar before pouring the brine. This customization lets you tailor the heat level to your family’s taste.
  8. For a milder version, omit the red pepper flakes and reduce the mustard seeds slightly. The subtle spice still adds complexity without heat, making it perfect for kids or those sensitive to spice.
  9. Always use clean utensils when removing peppers from the jar to avoid contamination. This simple habit keeps your pickles fresh longer and prevents spoilage.

  • 1 teaspoon baking soda

  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 cup grated zucchini, squeezed dry
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice
  • For lemon pudding glaze: 1 cup lemon pudding (prepared and cooled), 1/4 cup powdered sugar

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease or line a 9x5 inch loaf pan with parchment paper. This step ensures your bread won’t stick and the heat is evenly distributed for a perfect bake. Make sure the oven is fully preheated before putting the bread in to avoid uneven rising or dense texture.
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. Sifting or whisking these dry ingredients helps distribute the leavening agents evenly, so your bread rises uniformly without any bitter pockets of baking soda.
  3. In a large bowl, cream the softened butter and granulated sugar together until light and fluffy. This aeration step is key to a tender crumb and helps the bread rise nicely. Use room temperature butter for best results and don’t rush this step.
  4. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract. Adding eggs gradually helps maintain the emulsion and prevents the batter from curdling, which could lead to a dense loaf.
  5. Fold in the grated zucchini, lemon zest, and lemon juice gently. The zucchini adds moisture and texture, while the lemon zest and juice brighten the flavor. Be careful not to overmix here to keep the bread tender.
  6. Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just combined. Overmixing at this stage develops gluten and can make the bread tough, so stop as soon as no flour streaks remain.
  7. Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan and smooth the top with a spatula. This helps ensure even baking and a nice shape. Tap the pan lightly on the counter to release any air bubbles.
  8. Bake in the preheated oven for 45-50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. The bread should be golden brown and firm to the touch. Avoid opening the oven door too early to prevent collapse.
  9. Allow the bread to cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. While still warm, spread the lemon pudding glaze evenly over the top. The glaze will soak in slightly, adding moisture and a glossy finish. Let the bread cool completely before slicing.

  • 1 cup diced bell peppers (red and yellow)
  • 1/2 cup diced red onion
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon dried Italian herbs
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Fresh basil or parsley for garnish

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). While it heats, slice the zucchinis lengthwise and use a spoon to carefully scoop out the seeds and some flesh to create boats about 1/2 inch thick. This step is crucial because it gives the zucchini enough space to hold the filling without becoming mushy during baking. Be gentle to avoid breaking the boats. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and lightly brush the insides with olive oil, then sprinkle with salt and pepper. This prepares the zucchini to roast evenly and develop a tender texture with a slight caramelized edge. Avoid skipping the oil here as it helps prevent sticking and adds flavor.
  2. In a mixing bowl, toss the cherry tomatoes, diced bell peppers, red onion, and minced garlic with olive oil, dried Italian herbs, salt, and pepper. Spread this mixture onto a separate baking sheet and roast in the oven for 15 minutes until the veggies are tender and caramelized. Roasting the filling separately intensifies the flavors and prevents the zucchini from releasing too much moisture, which could make the boats soggy. If you rush this step or skip roasting the filling, the texture will be less vibrant and the flavors won’t meld as well. The vegetables should have a slight char and soft texture when done.
  3. Spoon the roasted vegetable mixture evenly into each zucchini boat, packing it gently but not too tightly. This step ensures every bite is filled with flavorful veggies and that the boats hold their shape during the final bake. Overstuffing can cause the filling to spill over and undercook, while underfilling might result in dry zucchini. Aim for a generous but balanced amount.
  4. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese evenly over the stuffed zucchini boats. The cheese adds a creamy, melty topping that contrasts beautifully with the tender vegetables. Using mozzarella gives a mild, gooey finish, but you can experiment with other cheeses if you prefer. The cheese also helps bind the filling together as it melts during baking.
  5. Return the stuffed zucchini boats to the oven and bake at 400°F (200°C) for another 10-15 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and starting to brown. This final bake melts the cheese perfectly and allows the flavors to meld. Keep an eye on the cheese to avoid burning; if it browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil.
  6. Once baked, remove the zucchini boats from the oven and let them rest for 5 minutes. This resting time helps the filling set slightly so it doesn’t spill out when serving. It also allows the flavors to settle and the cheese to firm up just enough for a perfect bite.
  7. Garnish the zucchini boats with freshly chopped basil or parsley for a bright, fresh contrast to the roasted flavors. Adding fresh herbs at the end lifts the dish visually and adds a pleasant herbal aroma that complements the vegetables and cheese.
  8. Serve the zucchini boats warm with a simple side salad or crusty bread to make a complete meal. The combination of textures and flavors makes this dish satisfying without needing meat. It’s perfect for a cozy dinner or a light lunch.
  9. If you want to prepare ahead, assemble the zucchini boats up to the cheese topping and refrigerate them covered for up to 24 hours. When ready to serve, bake as directed, adding a few extra minutes if chilled. This makes it a great make-ahead meal for busy days.

This hot brine is key to quick pickling because it penetrates the cucumber slices rapidly, infusing them with flavor and preserving their crispness. If you skip this step or rush it, the pickles won’t develop their signature tangy flavor as well.
  3. Place the drained cucumbers and onions into a clean heatproof jar or bowl. Pour the hot brine over the vegetables, making sure they are completely submerged. Stir gently to distribute the spices evenly. Let the mixture cool to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. The longer they sit, the more flavorful they become, but even after an hour, they’re deliciously tangy and crunchy.
  4. After the pickles have chilled, taste and add fresh chopped dill if desired. Dill adds a fresh herbal note that complements the sweet and sour flavors beautifully. Stir gently to combine. Store the pickles in the refrigerator and consume within 2 weeks for best texture and flavor.

  8. Make sure to use a non-reactive container like glass or food-safe plastic for pickling. Metal containers can react with the vinegar and alter the flavor negatively.
  9. For best flavor, let the pickles rest overnight in the fridge if you can wait. This resting time allows the flavors to meld and the pickles to become more vibrant and balanced.

  • 4 cloves garlic, smashed
  • 2 tablespoons mustard seeds
  • 2 teaspoons dill seeds

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by washing your cucumbers thoroughly to remove any dirt or residue. Slice them into spears about 3 to 4 inches long, making sure they are fairly uniform for even pickling. Place the sliced cucumbers in a large bowl of ice water and let them soak for at least 30 minutes. This soaking step helps to firm up the cucumbers by drawing out excess moisture, which is key to getting that satisfying crunch in the final canned pickles. Avoid skipping this step or using warm water, as it can result in softer pickles. After soaking, drain the cucumbers well and pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel to remove any excess water.
  2. While the cucumbers soak, prepare the pickling brine by combining white vinegar, water, and kosher salt in a large pot. Bring this mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally to dissolve the salt completely. The vinegar provides the essential acidity to preserve the pickles and develop their tangy flavor, while the salt enhances taste and helps maintain crispness. Boiling the brine ensures the flavors meld and sterilizes the solution for safe canning. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and keep the brine warm until ready to pour over the cucumbers. Do not rush this step by pouring cold brine over the cucumbers, as it can affect texture and preservation.
  3. Prepare your canning jars by washing them in hot, soapy water and rinsing thoroughly. To sterilize, place the jars in a large pot of boiling water for 10 minutes or run them through a hot dishwasher cycle. Sterilized jars prevent contamination and ensure your pickles stay fresh longer. Keep the jars warm until filling to avoid cracking when hot brine is added. Also, prepare the lids and bands by simmering them in hot water (do not boil) to soften the sealing compound.
  4. Add a couple of garlic cloves, a tablespoon of mustard seeds, a teaspoon of dill seeds, and a few black peppercorns to the bottom of each sterilized jar. These spices infuse the pickles with classic tangy and aromatic flavors. Avoid overfilling the jars with spices, which can overpower the cucumbers. Place a fresh dill sprig on top of the spices in each jar for a bright herbal note. This layering ensures the flavors distribute evenly during the pickling process.
  5. Pack the drained cucumber spears tightly into each jar, standing them upright if possible. Leave about 1/2 inch of headspace at the top to allow for expansion during processing and to ensure a proper seal. Overpacking can cause jars to crack or lids to fail, while underpacking wastes space and brine. Firm but gentle packing keeps the cucumbers intact and ready for pickling. Wipe the rims of the jars clean with a damp cloth to remove any residue that might interfere with sealing.
  6. Pour the hot brine carefully over the cucumbers in each jar, covering them completely while maintaining the 1/2 inch headspace. The hot brine helps to slightly soften the cucumbers and infuse them with flavor. Tap the jars gently to release any trapped air bubbles, which can cause spoilage if left inside. Use a non-metallic utensil to slide around the inside edges to dislodge bubbles. Wipe the rims again if needed before placing the lids on.
  7. Seal the jars with the sterilized lids and screw on the bands fingertip-tight. Do not over-tighten, as air must escape during processing. Place the jars in a boiling water bath canner, ensuring they are fully submerged by at least 1 inch of water. Process the jars for 10 minutes to create a vacuum seal and preserve the pickles safely. This step kills any bacteria and extends shelf life. After processing, carefully remove the jars and place them on a towel to cool undisturbed for 12 to 24 hours.
  8. Once cooled, check the seals by pressing the center of each lid; it should not flex up or down. Label the jars with the date and store them in a cool, dark place for at least two weeks before opening to allow flavors to develop fully. This resting period is essential for the pickles to absorb the brine and become perfectly tangy and crisp. Refrigerate any jars that do not seal properly and consume within a few weeks.
  9. When ready to enjoy, open a jar and serve your homemade canned pickles chilled or at room temperature. They’re fantastic on sandwiches, burgers, or as a crunchy snack. Leftover opened jars should be refrigerated and eaten within a month for best quality. The pickles will maintain their crispness and tangy flavor for several months when stored unopened in a pantry. Enjoy the satisfaction of your homemade canned pickles any time of year!
